recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. These products work, not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton

recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He teaches occult symbolism and tarot on his YouTube channel, ranging across the Major Arcana, the esoteric Enneagram, mythology and archetype, mystic linguistics, and the symbolism hidden in popular film. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Name: Gabe (Slick Dissident)
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Role: Co-host of Vibe Rant; teacher of occult symbolism & tarot

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Music as Elevation and Cultural Influence", "body": "One of the hosts argued that certain kinds of music had been deliberately engineered to lower human consciousness, while people in the past used music to lift their minds toward a spiritual ideal or a shared social harmony. Oliver Brusca said festival audiences told him his music felt refreshing against a backdrop of dark, heavy sounds, and he spoke of the endless possibility in production. Later, one of the hosts relayed a podcast claim that tempo changes heart rate and that classical music helped plants grow, then questioned what heavily promoted mainstream music was doing to listeners."}, {"title": "Choosing Music With No Plan B", "body": "Oliver Brusca recalled finding music production in high school and feeling it was his truest expression. He said that watching older coworkers at an insurance job convinced him to commit with no plan B, so he took freelance web design and night shifts at a grocery store while living month to month. He credited steady showing up, Ashtanga yoga and breath work for his flow states. One of the hosts argued that rehearsing a mental to do list drained energy. Oliver also said he tried to stay fluid and not over identify with being a music guy."}, {"title": "Protective Visualization and Night Experiences", "body": "Oliver Brusca described waking to disturbing night experiences and teaching himself to hold his ground by picturing a sphere of light and refusing fear. Gabe said the projection of will was one of the keys, and that the dreamer could call the shots. Chance said the same mindset worked outside of sleep, and that reading everyday events like dream analysis changed his life. One of the hosts argued that visualization was a real energetic form. Oliver added that during a difficult psychedelic experience, body shapes and mudras reshaped his surroundings, deepening his respect for yoga."}, {"title": "Entities, Festivals and Reasoning With Fear", "body": "One of the hosts described a festival memory from an altered state in which hooded figures appeared to send small shadowy creatures onto intoxicated people, and said he could not rule out intentional psychic interference. Oliver replied that festival crowds were energetically open and vulnerable. Later, one speaker argued that adversarial entities could be reasoned with, saying that Satan means adversary and that serving non existence made no sense. Chance said that on rare occasions, touching the ancestral river with a tuning fork brought a message to mind."}, {"title": "Tarot, Mugwort and Eclipse Season Stories", "body": "One of the hosts pulled five cards for Oliver, reading the Magician, a reversed High Priestess and Temperance as a path toward fearless creative balance, and Oliver said it captured his arc. Gabe linked Artemisia to Temperance and called mugwort dream medicine, while Oliver said he had brewed and burned it. Gabe called his eclipse season intense, and Jorge said he felt settled and grounded. Oliver described a mountain lion at his door on a full moon night, and a host read animal medicine about the cat."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Oliver Brusca is the man behind the music of VOLO, who has crafted an ethereal selection of uplifting and artful audio odysseys. Tonight we'll discover what makes his metronome tick and explore thoughts on the role of music in society. Joining us once again is the greatest bassist in our band, music theory teacher and podcaster Jorge Mesa.
